rationale: Implements the C2PA standard directly: embeds signed, tamper-evident provenance/history metadata into media assets, which is metadata watermarking for content authenticity applied in practice.
Bundles multiple published LLM watermarking schemes, several explicitly designed to survive paraphrase/removal attacks, as a common toolkit for applying and comparing them.
Directly implements metadata/token-level watermark embedding for LLM-generated text, the core mechanism this question asks about.
Standardized benchmark for comparing deepfake detector robustness across models and datasets, directly usable to empirically assess how detectors hold up as generative methods advance.
Deployable multi-model ensemble detector meant to be run in practice (Docker services + API), not a single research checkpoint -- directly implements a deepfake-content-detection pipeline.

A deployable AI-text detector explicit about its own confidence/robustness limits (refuses to overstate weak evidence on short text), directly relevant to the question of how reliable such detectors can be expected to be.
Automates license detection/collection across a codebase's own source and its dependencies, directly usable to automate license collection before training.
Scans source trees to verify declared license/copyright, useful for auditing accuracy when aggregating datasets sourced from multiple places.
